summary: Challis National Forest L-4 cabin built 1933 and gone by 1967; sources differ on removed or destroyed. A 2019 climbing guide describes remnants at the summit.

facts.status_note: Cabin removed or destroyed in 1967. A 2019 climbing guide photo caption describes remnants of the lookout on the summit.

staffing.status: No staff named in any source; Idaho Fire Lookouts says no staffing history is documented

access.note: Reached by forest roads; a 4WD vehicle is recommended. No source describes a closure or permit rule.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. The climbing guide says to park just below the summit after the forest-road drive.

events.note: L-4 cabin, per the register and three other sites. Forest Lookouts Idaho page says 'L-4 hip-roof'.
Register says the cabin was removed in 1967.
Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts Idaho page say destroyed in 1967.

evidence.quote: Built in 1933, this L-4 cabin was removed in 1967.
This L-4 cab, built in 1933, was destroyed in 1967.
We don't yet have a documented staffing history for this lookout.
1933: An L-4 hip-roof lookout cabin constructed.
Feltham Creek Point is located roughly 21 miles northwest of Stanley, Idaho.
This peak is a former fire lookout site.
The remnants of the lookout atop Feltham Crek Point looking east.
The view from the summit is exceptional and includes the Sawtooths

corrections.why: Four sources give 1933 as the build year, and the record has no build event.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says the cabin was removed in 1967. Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts Idaho page say destroyed in 1967. All agree the cabin was gone by 1967.
Firelookout.com says 21 miles north of Stanley; the climbing guide says roughly 21 miles northwest of Stanley.
Register gives 8,996 ft (2,742 m). Idaho Fire Lookouts and the climbing guide give 9,000 ft.

sources.title: Feltham Creek Point Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Build year 1933 and the 1967 end date agree across sources; removed versus destroyed is the only disagreement. No source names staff or notable fires. Remnants rest on one climbing-guide photo caption (2019). Access level public is inferred from the drive-up tag and the forest-road route; no source states an access rule. Elevation in the record (2742 m) matches the register. Fact-check 2026-10-09: no factual errors; reworded three sentences that copied quote wording; added evidence for the 2019 date and the forest-road route.
